text.p: Emery Worldwide plans to become the number one transportation and logistics company in Latin America and will add offices and employees to reach that goal, an Emery executive said Wednesday.

"We need to have a large presence and will have a large presence in the major countries in Latin America," said Ron Young, vice president, Latin America area. Emery, based in Redwood City, Calif., is a subsidiary of Consolidated Freightways Inc.

The Latin American sector is growing rapidly for Emery. Its volumes shipped grew 43 percent in 1994, 23 percent in 1995 and for the first nine months, Emery has handled 109 percent more tons than the same period of 1995, Young said.

Emery, which has specialized in shipping garments, perishables, and products for the auto industry, will next target pharmaceuticals, electronics and construction, energy and heavy equipment, Young said.

The company will open more offices, convert more agencies to Emery offices and increase its 40 person sales force, he said. Until 1991, Emery operated only through agencies when it changed three offices in Mexico to company operations. In 1995 Santiago and Buenos Aires followed.
"We also see good opportunities for business inside Latin America," said Young, specifically referring to the Mercosur countries.
Currently 60 percent of Emery's Latam business is from North Amercia, the rest is transhipments or shipping within the region.

Emery operates as a freight forwarder in Latin America and has been in the region for more than 20 years, Young said. It is also expanding its ocean business and will begin shipping by ocean to Latin America in December.

Young is also studying the feasibility of opening a "super center" in Miami to add logistics capabilities for its customers with Latin American business. This would involve tripling warehouse space from the current 36,000 square feet to 110,000 square feet. In Latin America, Emery's typical shipment is a 500 pound finished manufactured item, said Young. Emery handles the most hung garments of any forwarder in Latin America, Young said.
Despite the plans for expansion, Emery does not anticipate flying its own aircraft in Latin America as it does inside the United States.

"As long as there is capacity and our needs are being met, we don't see any need to fly our own planes," said Young. Emery does fly charters to Latin America. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+44 171 542-5017
